answer: The cheapest real defence: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because saffron only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, knoll is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any onyx approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
